## Authentic delivery and assessment materials {#o017-wrap-index}

The nine units of *Traceable Mathematical Work* remain the sole narrative
spine for O017/D120. This document does not replace or abridge them, nor does it
add a tenth unit. It supplies the delivery contract needed to follow the book's
local exercises and synthetic cases with evidence of authentic work. All five
assessment families below are required and **cannot compensate for one
another**.

The accompanying calibration package uses real mathematical sources, but all
learners, evaluators, seminars, review cycles, and transactions within that
package are synthetic. The package demonstrates the form of good evidence; it
is not evidence that a learner or community ever carried out those events, and
it never awards credit.

The canonical machine-readable definitions are in
[`o017-delivery-definitions.json`](../delivery/definitions/o017-delivery-definitions.json),
the submission schema is in
[`o017-delivery.schema.json`](../delivery/schema/o017-delivery.schema.json),
and complete examples are in the
[calibration package](../delivery/calibration/calibration-package.json).

These requirements govern learner assessment. They are not human-dependent
conditions on preparing, validating, or publishing this teaching edition.

### No-contact and no-transmission rules {#o017-wrap-no-contact}

This wrapper, its renderers and checkers, and local evaluators may prepare,
check, and retain packages locally. They **must not** send messages, open
issues, upload files, complete forms, register seminars, or contact outside
people or communities without separate human authorization specific to one
named transaction. Mathematical suitability, `prepared` status, or a passing
local assessment does not authorize transmission.

A transaction authorization must specify at least the target, artifact,
version to be sent, channel, responsible human sender, personal-data boundary,
and validity period. A missing field means `authorization_present = false`.
Authorization must not be inherited from another task or inferred from a
general desire to contribute.

External records may assert only events supported by evidence. A local draft
is `prepared`, not `submitted`. A system receipt can support `acknowledged`
status, but not `accepted`. The statuses `accepted`, `merged`, and `published`
each require a different event witness. If the external state cannot be
determined, use `unknown` while retaining the last proven state.

### Evaluator identity and privacy {#o017-wrap-evaluator-privacy}

An assessment package uses opaque evaluator IDs, such as
`O017-WRAP-EVAL-7F3K9Q`, rather than names, email addresses, account names, or
student numbers. Generate IDs randomly; do not derive them from hashes of
names or email addresses. Where genuinely necessary, a trusted administrator
keeps the mapping from IDs to real identities separately in encrypted,
access-controlled storage. That mapping does not belong in the portfolio,
repository, or public package.

For a two-person cycle, the administrator creates this record:

`evaluator_distinctness_attestation`

It states only that the two IDs represent two different humans and that
conflicts of interest have been checked. The
attestation does not reveal identities. Agents, models, or one person changing
roles may be used for practice, but they do not satisfy the independence gate.

## Five required assessment families {#o017-wrap-assessments}

### A01 — Real-source search {#o017-wrap-a01-real-source-search}

The learner starts with a mathematical question, not a supplied list of
sources. They conduct a search without pre-seeded candidates, then freeze at
least one real paper or monograph. The package must contain:

1. the question and topic boundary before searching;
2. queries, services used, and retrieval times;
3. every candidate admitted to the comparison, not just the winner;
4. assessment of primary authority, version/edition, locators, access rights,
   and relationships among sources;
5. a stopping rule written before the final conclusion;
6. a persistent identifier or authoritative URL, access date, and byte witness
   or version witness where available; and
7. uncertainties and reasons for excluding candidates.

A pass is not determined by the number of results. The gate is traceability
from question to query, query to candidates, and candidates to the exact
frozen source appropriate to the claim that will be used.

### A02 — Real seminar or supervised equivalent {#o017-wrap-a02-seminar}

The main pathway is to attend or deliver a real mathematics seminar. Minimum
evidence comprises the event identity, date and time zone, learner's role,
timed or segmented notes, dependency map, question log, privacy-minimizing
evidence of attendance or delivery, corrected final notes, and an explicit
distinction between what was heard, what was inferred, and what was verified
only after the event.

If live audio/video is inaccessible because of disability, bandwidth, time
zone, safety, or the absence of an available event, a supervised equivalent
may use a recording and official transcript/notes from a real mathematics
seminar or lecture. A human supervisor must assign the segments, check the
dependency map and question log, and attest that the learner did the work.
This pathway is assessed with the same criteria and recorded as follows:

`supervised_equivalent`

It is not claimed as live attendance.

An access alternative must not depend on audio alone. Provide structured text,
section or time locators, formulas in text/MathML/LaTeX, descriptions of visual
information, and a way to submit questions without speaking live.

### A03 — Two-person author–referee cycle {#o017-wrap-a03-referee-cycle}

Two different humans take the author and referee roles. The package preserves:

- the frozen initial manuscript and its hash;
- the referee's scope and conflict-of-interest statement;
- a report mapping every comment to a locator and evidence;
- the author's response to each comment;
- a disposition table using `accepted`, `partially_accepted`,
  `rejected_with_reason`, or *unresolved*;
- the revision, before-and-after comparison, and new hash; and
- a list of issues still open.

One person playing both roles, two accounts belonging to the same person, or
automated review without a human referee constitute practice, not evidence of
a passing assessment. Style scores cannot compensate for failures of
mathematical validity, independence, or revision traceability.

### A04 — Real-source erratum dossier {#o017-wrap-a04-erratum}

The learner freezes a real open source at a particular edition or
representation, identifies the defect locator, separates the statement's
status from a conjecture about its cause, supplies a minimal reproducer,
assesses severity and confidence separately, offers the smallest possible
correction, and audits downstream consequences. A second human performs an
independent mathematical check and marks the parts checked, method, result,
and limitations.

An already published correction can still support an audit if the learner
freezes the older version, reproduces the diagnosis independently, and then
uses the official correction as a comparison. The dossier must not claim a
new discovery. Without a second human checker, the highest status is
`ready_for_review`.

### A05 — Community transaction or weaker local pathway {#o017-wrap-a05-community}

The `community_transaction` pathway requires specific authorization before
transmission. The learner sends one concise, nonduplicative, reviewable
contribution that follows the target's rules. Passing does not require
acceptance; evidence of authorized submission is sufficient, provided later
status remains truthful. The ledger uses `prepared`, `submitted`,
`acknowledged`, `accepted`, `merged`, `published`, `rejected`, `withdrawn`, or
`unknown` and does not erase history.

If external action is unsafe, unavailable, or unauthorized, an independent
human may assess the real-source package locally. This result is labelled
`externally_reviewed_local`. It satisfies the weaker A05 branch, but it is
**not** evidence of submission or community participation. The final
credential must retain that label. The calibration package demonstrates this
pathway and stops at `prepared`; no contact or transmission occurs.

## Noncompensable gates {#o017-wrap-gates}

All nine gates below must be `pass`. A high numerical score on other gates
cannot substitute for them.

| ID | Gate | Minimum passing condition |
|---|---|---|
| `O017-WRAP-G01` | Source and version | Real, authoritative source with locators and a frozen version/representation. |
| `O017-WRAP-G02` | Search provenance | Complete queries, times, candidates, stopping rule, selection, and uncertainties. |
| `O017-WRAP-G03` | Seminar context | Real event or supervised equivalent with evidence and the correct pathway label. |
| `O017-WRAP-G04` | Human independence | Two opaque IDs represent two different humans; attestation and conflict-of-interest check are available. |
| `O017-WRAP-G05` | Mathematical validity | Claims, reproducer/proof, diagnosis, correction, and limitations are checked against the frozen version. |
| `O017-WRAP-G06` | Critique–revision chain | Initial manuscript, report, response, dispositions, revision, and before-and-after evidence are traceable. |
| `O017-WRAP-G07` | Status and authorization | No external status without evidence; no transmission without specific authorization. |
| `O017-WRAP-G08` | Privacy and access | Personal data are minimized and equivalent access alternatives are available and actually tested. |
| `O017-WRAP-G09` | Evidence manifest | Every artifact has an ID, locator, byte count, hash, rights statement, verification status, and retention owner. |

Any `fail`, `not_evaluated`, or `unknown` prevents an assessment pass.
`not_applicable` is valid only for criteria that do not apply under the branch
definition; it cannot be used for any of the nine gates above.

## Results and credentials {#o017-wrap-credential}

Each of A01–A05 is assessed separately. The overall decision can only be:

- `complete_community_transaction`: A01–A05 pass and A05 has evidence of
  `submitted` or a later event;
- `complete_externally_reviewed_local`: A01–A04 pass and the local A05 branch
  passes with an independent human reviewer;
- `incomplete`: at least one family or noncompensable gate has not passed; or
- `calibration_only`: a demonstration package that must not award credit.

Acceptance, merging, or publication of a contribution is not required for
passing and does not automatically add to the score. A documented rejection
can remain consistent with a pass when package quality, authorization, and
truthful status reporting have passed. Conversely, a contribution that happens
to be accepted does not compensate for failures of rights, privacy, or
independence.

## Using the machine-readable package {#o017-wrap-machine-package}

1. Copy the example's structure without copying its calibration claims as
   learner data.
2. Create new stable package, submission, attempt, evaluator, and evidence IDs.
3. Freeze all artifacts; record their byte counts and SHA-256 in the manifest.
4. Validate JSON against the schema and CSV as UTF-8 with exact headers.
5. Have evaluators determine every criterion and gate; do not compute averages
   before all noncompensable gates pass.
6. Issue a credential only after the A05 branch label and external status
   match the evidence.
7. Keep the event ledger append-only. A correction adds a new event; it does
   not overwrite history.

The
[calibration package](../delivery/calibration/calibration-package.json)
provides one complete example for each family. All person references are
synthetic IDs, all events are simulations, every `credit_eligible` value is
**false**, and every `transmission_performed` value is **false**.

## Primary sources for calibration {#o017-wrap-calibration-sources}

Calibration uses the following official open sources without claiming
endorsement from their publishers or instructors:

- OpenStax, *Calculus Volume 1*, §5.3, official publisher page and CC BY-NC-SA
  4.0 license:
  <https://openstax.org/books/calculus-volume-1/pages/5-3-the-fundamental-theorem-of-calculus>;
- MIT OpenCourseWare 18.100A, Lecture 22, Fall 2020, official page and CC
  BY-NC-SA 4.0 license:
  [official Lecture 22 page](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-100a-real-analysis-fall-2020/resources/18100a-lecture-22-multicam/);
- G. H. Hardy, “Addenda and Corrigenda”, *Proceedings of the London Mathematical
  Society* (1928), version-of-record DOI
  <https://doi.org/10.1112/plms/s2-28.1.553-t>.

The calibration text paraphrases metadata and carries out its own
mathematical calculations; it does not copy source layouts, images, videos, or
prose. When a component's redistribution rights are not sufficiently clear,
the package retains only its citation, bibliographic facts, locators, and
original analysis.
